evidence: Type inventory (counted from frozen judge.toml files): gates/render 1 binary, gates/constraints 1 binary (both aggregation all_pass, as the gate contract requires); scored/functional 44/44 binary, weighted_mean with weights 0.5-2.5; scored/polish 5/5 binary, weighted_mean with weights 1.5-3; scored/visual 5/5 likert, points = 5, weight 1.2 each. This matches the template's shipped format (template visual is likert points=5; functional/polish binary). (1) Pass/fail behaviours are binary: every functional row is a verifiable product rule with an explicit failure clause (e.g. functional/judge.toml:47 hro_add_email_rules 'Fails if a duplicate or invalid address is saved...'); a keyword scan for craft wording (clear/readable/polished/quality/intuitive/legible) in functional found only 'readable line naming who and what changed' (line 272, hro_activity), which is a presence/content check, not a degree-of-quality judgement. Polish rows are behavioural state-preservation checks under concurrency, not aesthetics: polish/prompt.md:14 'Judge how the workspace holds up while people work at the same time, not visual craft'; e.g. polish/judge.toml:23 hro_pol_live_board requires note text, activeElement and scroll offset to be preserved (measured via page.evaluate) - a yes/no observable, so binary fits; gradation comes from five separately weighted rows. (2) Craft is likert with described anchors at every level: visual/judge.toml hro_vis_type 25-29, hro_vis_color 40-44, hro_vis_layout 55-59, hro_vis_hierarchy 70-74, hro_vis_consistency 85-89 each give explicit 5/4/3/2/1 anchors; visual/prompt.md:12 and :7 define floor behaviour (raw Likert 1, normalised zero) consistently with the polish prompt's binary0 wording (polish/prompt.md:12,18). Per SKILL.md:65 and quality-checks.md:170 the Internal sheet note ('Likert we dont use in rewardkit') is a known false positive; judged against shipped format, there are no binary craft rows and no likert rows missing anchors. Counterexample attempts: (a) a broken app that partially preserves state (keeps the note but resets scroll) gets 0 on hro_pol_live_board rather than partial credit, but this is a binary behaviour with a stated conjunctive bar, and its other polish rows still score independently - not lost craft gradation; (b) a conforming alternative with an unconventional but deliberate visual style is not penalised by anchors, which are style-neutral and visual/prompt.md:14 states 'Layout, labels and styles are the implementer's choice'. Neither yields a defect for this row. Limitation (not a waiver): no configured judge run exists (raw-evidence-index scope: 'Full configured grading/workload, reward discrimination/ranking and Oracle/target scores are absent'), so how the judge actually distributes likert scores is unmeasured; that is the concern of rows 40/42 and the runtime records, not of this static type-fit row.
